findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on the datetime key it is used with
findings.body:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit log endpoint uses it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime`. `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result, which raises `TypeError` and returns a 500 for any non-empty page.

`value_from_cursor` (line 843) has a related problem. It returns the raw integer cursor value, and `build_queryset` then emits `datetime <= <int>`, which Postgres rejects.

The optimized path is therefore unusable. It needs the `DateTimePaginator` key/cursor conversion, e.g. by subclassing `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django; comment's safety claim is false
findings.body:
When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"). Any admin-supplied cursor with a negative offset, e.g. `?cursor=0:-5:0`, therefore produces a 500.

The comments state the ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically" and that this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". Both are wrong, and the second describes an intent to bypass pagination bounds that should not ship. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as the other paginators do.

findings.title: AttributeError on default path when organization_context.member is None
findings.body:
`enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally, even when `optimized_pagination` was not requested, and dereferences `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None` for callers that are not org members, such as staff sessions and API-key/token authenticated requests.

For these callers `request.user.is_superuser` is False, so the expression raises `AttributeError` and the endpoint returns 500. This is a regression to the existing, non-optimized audit log listing. Only evaluate this when `use_optimized` is true, and guard for `member is None`.

findings.title: Privilege gate uses raw is_superuser flag instead of active superuser session
findings.body:
The gate uses `request.user.is_superuser`, which is true for any account with the superuser flag. It does not check whether the superuser session is active (sudo/elevated). Sentry's convention is `is_active_superuser(request)`.

As written, a flagged user with no active superuser session who has org access gets the "admin-only" pagination behaviour.

findings.title: Spans are silently evicted with no metric or log
findings.body:
Before this change, oversized segments were detected at flush time and reported via the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric plus `logger.error`. That check was removed from `_load_segment_data`.

The new `zpopmin` eviction in the Lua script drops the lowest-scored spans whenever a segment exceeds 1000. Nothing is returned to the caller and nothing is emitted, so span data is lost with no observability.

The script should return the evicted count so Python can emit a metric, or the old metric should be kept in some form.

findings.title: max_segment_spans config is now dead; limit hardcoded in Lua with a different value
findings.body:
`SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans` (default 1001), but nothing reads it anymore. The actual cap is the literal `1000` hardcoded in `add-buffer.lua`.

Callers that tune `max_segment_spans` will see no effect, and the default disagrees with the enforced value. Pass the limit to the script as an ARGV, or remove the parameter.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE uses default SUM aggregate, corrupting scores on duplicate payloads
findings.body:
`zunionstore set_key 2 set_key span_key` (and the parent_key merge on line 53) uses the default `AGGREGATE SUM`. If the same payload is present in both sets, its score becomes the sum of two timestamps (~3.4e9), for example after a Kafka redelivery of a span.

That inflated score makes the duplicate effectively unevictable and breaks the end-timestamp ordering that `zpopmin` relies on. Use `AGGREGATE MAX` (or `MIN`) to keep scores meaningful.

findings.title: Evicted spans leave stale entries in the redirect hash
findings.body:
`zpopmin` removes payloads from the segment set, but their `span_id -> set_span_id` entries in `span-buf:sr:{...}` are never removed. `done_flush_segments` only `hdel`s the span IDs of spans actually flushed.

Since the redirect hash's TTL is refreshed on every insert for the trace, these entries linger. Late children of an evicted span can also be redirected into an already-flushed segment key.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit silently reduced 10x and explanatory comment removed
findings.body:
The redirect-following loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000. The comment explaining that trees deeper than the limit may not be joined correctly was also deleted.

This behaviour change is unrelated to eviction and is not mentioned in the PR. Segment trees deeper than 1000 levels will now be split into separate segments.

findings.title: No tests for span eviction or the new optimized audit-log pagination
findings.body:
The tests were only updated to pass `end_timestamp_precise`. Nothing exercises the new core behaviour: inserting more than 1000 spans into a segment and asserting which spans are evicted (lowest end timestamp), including across merges via `zunionstore`.

Likewise there are no tests for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or the `optimized_pagination=true` audit log path. Even a basic test would have caught that the path crashes on its datetime key.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offset support but no code changed
findings.body:
The new comment says negative offsets are allowed for "efficient reverse pagination". `Cursor` was already doing a plain `int(offset)`, and no behaviour changed.

The similar comment added in `BasePaginator.get_result` (paginator.py line 179) is also misleading. A negative offset with `is_prev` is still passed straight to the queryset slice, which raises in Django.

These comments misdocument the pagination contract and should be removed.
